[1]
parts.solution_md:
a)

i) The ionic equation for the reaction at the negative electrode is:

Al<sup>3+</sup> + 3e<sup>–</sup> → Al

- Al<sup>3+</sup>; **[1 mark]**
- Remainder of the ionic equation;** [1 mark]**

ii) The ionic equation for the reaction at the positive electrode is:

2O<sup>2–</sup> → O<sub>2</sub> + 4e<sup>–</sup>  **   **
**OR **   
2O<sup>2–</sup> - 4e<sup>–</sup> → O<sub>2</sub>

- Correct products, i.e. O<sub>2</sub> with / without e<sup>–</sup> dependent on the equation given; **[1 mark]**

**AND **
Because (electrical) energy is supplied / given / taken in; **[1 mark]**

| **Bond** | **Bond Energy kJ / mol** |
|---|---|
| N-N | +158 |
| N$\equiv$N | +945 |
| O-H | +463 |
| O-O | +144 |

The structures of the reactants and products are shown.

![5-1-5a-h-hydrazine-reaction-figure-5-1](assets/037-5-1-5a-h-hydrazine-reaction-figure-5-1.png)

d) To calculate the bond enthalpy of the N-H bond:

- Energy change = sum of bonds broken - sum of bonds made; **[1 mark]**
- -789 = [(4 x N-H) + (1 x 158) + (4 x 463) + (2 x 144)] - [(1 x 945) + (8 x 463)]** **
**OR** 
4 x N-H = -789 - [(1 x 158) + (4 x 463) + (2 x 144)] + [(1 x 945) + (8 x 463)]; **[1 mark]**
- 4 x N-H = -789 - 2298 + 4649; **[1 mark]**
- N-H bond enthalpy = 1562 ÷ 4 = (+)391 (kJ / mol); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *This bond energy calculation is very challenging however if you set out the question step by step you can gain 3 out of 4 marks just by showing logical working*
- *Careful:** A lot of students lose the last mark in this question because they forget that there are 4 N-H bonds in hydrazine, so the final answer needs to be divided by 4 to get the individual bond enthalpy for each N-H bond *

#### Extended Only

Propanol reacts with methanoic acid to form the ester propyl methanoate.

CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH + HCOOH → HCOOCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O

i) Calculate the *M*<sub>r</sub> of methanoic acid = ........................................

[1]

ii) Calculate the *M*<sub>r</sub> of propanol = ........................................

[1]

iii) Determine which one is the limiting reagent. Show your reasoning.

[2]

iv) Calculate the maximum yield in grams of propyl methanoate, *M*<sub>r</sub> = 88.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
d) CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH + HCOOH → HCOOCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O

i) The *M*<sub>r</sub> of methanoic acid is:

- H + C + O + O + H = 1 + 12 + 16 + 16 + 1 = <u>46</u>; **[1 mark]**

ii) The *M*<sub>r</sub> of propanol is

- C + (3 x H) + C + (2 x H) + C + (2 x H) + O + H = 12 + 3 + 12 + 2 + 12 + 2 + 16 + 1 = <u>60</u>; **[1 mark]**

iii) To determine the limiting reagent:

- Moles of propanol = $=\frac{6.0}{60}=$0.1; **[1 mark]**
- Moles of methanoic acid $=\frac{4.0}{46}=$0.087 
**AND **
The limiting reagent is methanoic acid; **[1 mark]**

iv) The maximum yield in grams of propyl methanoate is:

- 88 x 0.087 = <u>7.65</u> (g); **[1 mark]** 
*Allow error carried forward from part (iii) using the lowest number of moles, i.e. 88 x lowest number of moles*

**[Total: 5 marks]**

- *To calculate the **M*<sub>*r*</sub>* of a chemical, add up all of the atomic masses for **ALL** of the atoms in the chemical*

  - *Careful: **Make sure that you don't miss any atoms as this will lead to an incorrect answer*
- *Remember: **In this reaction, the limiting reagent is the reactant with the fewest number of moles involved in the reaction as the reactants react in a 1:1 ratio*

  - *For this question, you calculate the number of moles using the equation moles = *$\frac{\mathrm{mass}}{M_{r}}$
- *The limiting reagent will determine the maximum amount of a product that can be formed*

  - *This is because once the limiting reagent is used up, you cannot form any more product*
- *The **M*<sub>*r*</sub>* of propyl methanoate, HCOOCH*<sub>*2*</sub>*CH*<sub>*2*</sub>*CH*<sub>*3*</sub>*, is 88 g / mol*

  - *The chemical equation shows that there is a 1 : 1 ratio between the either reactant and the propyl methanoate product*
  - *Therefore, the maximum yield will be the **M*<sub>*r*</sub>* of propyl methanoate multiplied by the number of moles of limiting reagent, e.g. 88 x 0.087 = 7.65 g*
